note: Grade 3. Spelling becomes rule-governed rather than sound-by-sound, and writing becomes something you come back to and change. Revision is the year's real subject.

skills.name: Spells longer words syllable by syllable
Spells words with prefixes and suffixes
Knows when to drop the e and change the y
skills.description: hope + ing = hoping. carry + ed = carried. Rules with clear edges, which makes them teachable.

skills.name: Keeps verb tense consistent
skills.description: Drifting between past and present mid-story is the usual error.

probe.prompt: Something changes halfway through. Find it.

skills.name: Matches the verb to the subject

probe.prompt: The dogs runs fast. Fix it.

skills.name: Uses apostrophes for belonging
skills.description: The dog's bone versus the dogs. Overuse on plurals is near universal.

probe.prompt: Whose bone is it? Write it.

skills.name: Starts a new paragraph when the topic changes

probe.prompt: Where should this break into paragraphs?

skills.name: Writes a paragraph where every sentence belongs

probe.prompt: Write a paragraph about {topic}. Every sentence should be about that one thing.

skills.name: Writes something with a beginning, middle, and end

probe.prompt: Write a story in three parts.

skills.name: Argues an opinion with reasons in order

probe.prompt: What do you think, and what are your three best reasons?

skills.name: Writes a short report on a topic

probe.prompt: Teach me about {topic} in a few paragraphs.

skills.name: Takes notes in their own words
skills.description: Not copying is the whole skill, and it has to be taught outright.

probe.prompt: Read this, then tell me the important bits without looking.

skills.name: Changes their writing after reading it back
skills.description: Moving, cutting, and rewriting rather than only adding. The hardest habit in this pack.

probe.prompt: Read it out loud. What would you move or take out?
Check it before anyone else does.
